top_entities.name: Jamaica
top_entities.news_summary: Jamaica's government signed contracts worth roughly $1 billion (JMD) on 2026-09-03 for delivery of 268 semi-permanent housing solutions (143 in Westmoreland, 125 in St Elizabeth) for families displaced by Hurricane Melissa (Oct 28 landfall; ~120,000 buildings lost roofs; ~US$8.8B physical damage per World Bank/IDB). Units financed via the National Housing Trust plus a housing donation from the Government of China. A moderate, dated, positive humanitarian/governance response.

top_entities.name: Boeing
top_entities.news_summary: FAA confirmed Boeing paid a $3,139,319 civil penalty (proposed September 2025) for quality-system violations connected to the January 2024 Alaska Airlines door-plug blowout (hundreds of violations at the 737 Renton plant and the Spirit AeroSystems Wichita fuselage facility, plus an employee pressuring an FAA-delegated co-worker to sign off a non-airworthy 737 MAX). Boeing paid this quietly in January 2026 without public disclosure; the payment only became public on 2026-09-02 via Reuters/AP wire coverage.

top_entities.name: Nepal
top_entities.news_summary: Nepal-Tibet border flash-flood/glacier-collapse disaster (originating 2026-08-26 on Langtang Lirung) death toll climbed to 1,114 in Nepal per an NDRRMA update reported Wednesday 2026-09-02 (plus 16 dead / ~546 missing on the Chinese side); ~3,916 missing in Nepal. A HiRISK report and CNN/ABC/Nature coverage (2026-09-01/09-02) found no glacier-hazard early-warning system existed for the affected area, that Nepal's SMS alert system failed or arrived late and Nepali-only, and satellite imagery showed visible glacier instability days before collapse -- a repeat of an unaddressed 2022 recommendation after a similar 2021 disaster. Community-based informal warning, not the official system, saved lives. NOTE: a later-aggregated figure of 1,259 dead / 5,083 missing appeared in search results (Wikipedia-sourced) but could not be tied to a dated primary source inside the window and is NOT used as the evidence figure here -- flagged per the superlative/death-toll verification discipline.

top_entities.name: Los Angeles
top_entities.news_summary: A House Oversight subcommittee (Rep. Burchett) summoned LA Mayor Karen Bass to testify Sept 15 over an alleged $1 billion LA Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) funding scandal. HUD's Inspector General has been investigating alleged failures in LAHSA's internal controls, financial management, and conflict-of-interest safeguards, and alleged repeated false statements; HUD's Deputy Secretary accused the agency of 'wanton mismanagement of public funds.' Separately, a federal judge ruled Aug 13 that HUD illegally revoked LAHSA funding given vulnerable unhoused residents depend on it. Reported via Hoodline, September 2026.

This is an AG enforcement action against a private landlord rather than direct city-agency misconduct, but it reflects DC housing-code enforcement activity in-window.
